3. The petitioner contested Suit No. 492 of 1981 by way of filing written statement denying all material allegations as contained in the plaint contending inter alia, that the suit is hopelessly barred by limitation, that the landlord Moharaja Shashi Kanta Acharjya Bahadur of Mymensingh being 16 annas owner settled the suit land in favour of the petitioner in 1347 BS on proper Nazar Salami and since then she has been owning and possessing the same in her own right and adversely against all others on payment of rent with the appropriate authority; the suit land being wrongly recorded in the Collector's Khas Khatian she filed the said Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970 in the 1st Court of Munsif Mymensingh under section 143(a) of the State Acquisition & Tenancy Act for correction of the ROR and the present plaintiff Government i.e. opposite party, contested the case by filing written objection; that on 09.01.71 when the Misc. Case was fixed for peremptory hearing, the opposite party government filed hazira but was found absent on repeated calls and the suit was taken up for hearing and after recording deposition of the petitioner and marking the relevant documents as exhibits the court was pleased to allow the said Misc. Case; that the opposite party Government had full knowledge of the said ex parte order dated 09.01.71; that the opposite party Government filed Misc. Case No. 23 of 1971 under Order 9 rule 13 CPC for setting aside the said ex parte order but the said Misc. Case No. 23 of 1971 was dismissed for default on 28.02.72 and thereafter the present plaintiff Government filed another Misc. Case No 72 of 1972 which was also dismissed on contest on 13.2.1973. 

 4. That on 11.2.86 when Suit No. 492 of 1981 was taken up for hearing the petitioner, as has been stated, being ill could not appear before the Court. The plaintiff-government examined only one witness Tahshilder Abdul Majid. It appears from the deposition of the said Tahshilder (Annexure 'A') that he says nothing about obtaining the ex parte order in Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970 fraudulently or by suppression of summons or by any other fraudulent means. 

 6. Mr. Gour Gopal Shaha, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner, submits that the suit was for declaration and cancellation of the ex parte order passed in Misc. Case No. 142 of 1970 and the suit is hopelessly time-barred inasmuch as the opposite party-government had full knowledge of the ex parte order dated 9.1.71.
